title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1970-02-27
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of the Feb 27 1970 Family Dog show, highlighted by Easy Wind, a blazing Not‑Fade‑Away→Lovelight transition and an ecstatic Lovelight finale.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about the crystal‑clear Charlie Miller transfer and the overall superb mix, calling it a must‑have for any 1970 collector. The performance is praised for its soaring Jerry Garcia leads, standout Easy Wind, the NFA→Lovelight segue and a wildly energetic Lovelight that caps a tight set. A few notes mention early‑night monitor glitches, but they do not detract from the overall brilliance of the show.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (10 out of 13) give 4‑5 stars and explicitly praise both the musical performance and the recording quality; only a couple of mixed/negative comments are present, yielding a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, balanced mix praised by multiple reviewers; Charlie Miller transfer highlighted as superb. A few early‑show monitor issues are noted, but the tape runs out only at the very end, preserving the performance.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider > High Time
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set builds smoothly from acoustic‑flavored numbers into high‑energy rock, peaking with the NFA→Lovelight transition and a pandemonium‑level Lovelight that leaves the audience buzzing.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers note Garcia at his finest – tight leads, soaring solos and an overall “finest stuff ever” vibe.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocals on Me and My Uncle are called melodic; backing vocal interplay with Pigpen gets special mention.
band_member_comments.Drums: No specific drum commentary beyond a brief note that separating the ‘Drums’ track was “absurd”.
